# rcnv_gene_associations_v

Gene-level rare-CNV association statistics from Collins et al. 2022, "A cross-disorder
dosage sensitivity map of the human genome" (Cell 185:3041-3055, doi
10.1016/j.cell.2022.06.036, CC-BY 4.0). One row per (phenotype, cnv_type, gene): 54 HPO
phenotype groups x {DEL, DUP} x 17,263 autosomal protein-coding genes, from a meta-analysis
of rare CNVs in 950,278 individuals. This is the per-phenotype counterpart to
dosage_sensitivity_v: that view says whether a gene is dosage sensitive in general, this one
says which phenotype a deletion or duplication of it is associated with. The gene's
pHaplo/pTriplo scores are joined onto every row here, so both questions are answerable
without a second query. SIGNIFICANCE HAS TWO TIERS, EACH GATED BY SECONDARY EVIDENCE. A gene
is exome-wide significant if `mlog10p > -LOG10(2.90e-6)` (P <= 2.90e-6), or FDR significant
if `mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01)` (FDR < 1%); either tier additionally requires at least one
of `n_nominal_cohorts >= 2` (nominal evidence in >= 2 independent cohorts) or
`mlog10p_secondary > -LOG10(0.05)` (the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis is still nominally
significant). Thresholding on `mlog10p` or `mlog10_fdr_q` alone, without the secondary-
evidence requirement, is not what the paper reports and will not reproduce its gene lists.
Checked against dev: the full rule — `(mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01) OR mlog10p >
-LOG10(2.90e-6)) AND (n_nominal_cohorts >= 2 OR mlog10p_secondary > -LOG10(0.05))` — returns
5,680 rows over 739 distinct genes, matching the paper's published totals. 65% OF ROWS ARE
"TESTED, NO ESTIMATE". Every gene appears for every phenotype and CNV type, including those
where the meta-analysis produced no estimate because no qualifying CNV was observed; those
rows carry NULL from `beta` onward. Filter `beta IS NOT NULL` to get the estimated
associations. Do NOT filter on `n_nominal_cohorts` for this — the NULL rows are not the rows
with n_nominal_cohorts = 0, and using it as a proxy silently drops real estimates.
PHENOTYPES ARE HPO GROUPS, WITH TWO SPECIAL CODES. `phenotype` is an HPO term id with the
colon removed (HP0012759 = HP:0012759). HP0000118 ("Phenotypic abnormality") is not a peer
of the other 53 codes — it is every case pooled (458,326 cases + 491,952 controls, the full
950,278-individual cohort), so it overlaps all the others and must not be summed with them.
UNKNOWN is the group of cases whose indication matched none of the listed HPO terms. For the
human-readable name, join phenotypes_v on `p.dataset = r.dataset AND p.trait_original =
r.phenotype` — this view calls its phenotype code `phenotype`, not `trait_original`. EFFECT
SIZES ARE ON THE LOG SCALE. `beta` is ln(odds ratio), so OR = EXP(beta), and
`beta_lower`/`beta_upper` are the 95% CI on the same scale. The `*_secondary` columns are a
leave-top-cohort-out sensitivity re-analysis (the meta re-run without `top_cohort`), NULL
for 86% of rows; use them to check that a signal is not carried by a single cohort, never as
the primary result. NO COORDINATES: the published data is GRCh37 and gene-keyed, so nothing
positional is stored here. Join gene_annotations_v on ensembl_gene_id for GRCh38
coordinates.

## Columns

| column | type | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dataset` | `STRING` | Source dataset, constant 'Collins_rCNV_2022' |
| `phenotype` | `STRING` | HPO phenotype group code without the colon (e.g. HP0012759). HP0000118 is all cases pooled; UNKNOWN is cases matching none of the listed terms. Join phenotypes_v.trait_original for the name |
| `cnv_type` | `STRING` | CNV class tested: DEL (deletion) or DUP (duplication) |
| `symbol` | `STRING` | Current HGNC gene symbol. NOT unique — join on ensembl_gene_id where the other side has it |
| `symbol_gencode_v19` | `STRING` | The symbol as published by Collins et al. (GENCODE v19 spelling) |
| `ensembl_gene_id` | `STRING` | Ensembl gene ID (e.g. ENSG00000251322). Part of the key (phenotype, cnv_type, ensembl_gene_id) and the join key to dosage_sensitivity_v and gene_annotations_v |
| `n_nominal_cohorts` | `INT64` | Number of contributing cohorts with nominal (P<0.05) evidence. One of the two ways to satisfy the paper's secondary-evidence requirement (n_nominal_cohorts >= 2, OR mlog10p_secondary > -LOG10(0.05)) alongside the primary FDR or exome-wide threshold. NOT a proxy for whether an estimate exists — use beta IS NOT NULL for that |
| `top_cohort` | `STRING` | Cohort contributing the strongest single-cohort signal; the one dropped in the *_secondary re-analysis |
| `cohorts_excluded` | `STRING` | Semicolon-separated cohorts excluded from this meta-analysis (too few cases for this phenotype, or no CNV data). NULL where none were excluded |
| `case_freq` | `FLOAT64` | Frequency of carriers of a qualifying CNV overlapping the gene among cases |
| `control_freq` | `FLOAT64` | Frequency of carriers of a qualifying CNV overlapping the gene among controls |
| `beta` | `FLOAT64` | Effect size as ln(odds ratio) — OR = EXP(beta). NULL where the gene was tested but no estimate was produced (65% of rows) |
| `beta_lower` | `FLOAT64` | Lower bound of the 95% CI on beta, ln scale |
| `beta_upper` | `FLOAT64` | Upper bound of the 95% CI on beta, ln scale |
| `z` | `FLOAT64` | Meta-analysis Z score |
| `mlog10p` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 of the meta-analysis p-value. Exome-wide significance in the paper is P <= 2.90e-6, i.e. mlog10p > -LOG10(2.90e-6), plus the secondary-evidence requirement on n_nominal_cohorts or mlog10p_secondary — see the view description |
| `mlog10_fdr_q` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 of the FDR q-value. The paper's FDR-significance threshold is FDR < 1%, i.e. mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01), plus the same secondary-evidence requirement — see the view description |
| `beta_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | beta from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis. NULL for 86% of rows |
| `beta_lower_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | Lower 95% CI bound of beta_secondary, ln scale |
| `beta_upper_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | Upper 95% CI bound of beta_secondary, ln scale |
| `z_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | Z score from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis |
| `mlog10p_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 p-value from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis |
| `mlog10_fdr_q_secondary` | `FLOAT64` | -log10 FDR q-value from the leave-top-cohort-out re-analysis |
| `phaplo` | `FLOAT64` | pHaplo for this gene, joined from dosage_sensitivity on ensembl_gene_id. Constant across the gene's rows |
| `ptriplo` | `FLOAT64` | pTriplo for this gene, joined from dosage_sensitivity on ensembl_gene_id. Constant across the gene's rows |
| `haploinsufficient` | `BOOL` | phaplo >= 0.86, the paper's haploinsufficiency cutoff |
| `triplosensitive` | `BOOL` | ptriplo >= 0.94, the paper's triplosensitivity cutoff |
| `resource` | `STRING` | Data source identifier, constant 'rcnv' — the same resource dosage_sensitivity_v carries |

## Columns with a small, enumerable set of values

| column | scoped by |
| --- | --- |
| `resource` | — |
| `dataset` | — |
| `cnv_type` | — |
| `phenotype` | — |

## Worked examples

Queries that run against rcnv_gene_associations_v as written.

### PheWAS for one gene across the 54 HPO groups: which phenotypes a deletion or duplication of it is associated with, strongest FDR first. The phenotype name comes from phenotypes_v, joined on trait_original = phenotype.

```sql
SELECT r.phenotype, p.trait_name, r.cnv_type, r.n_nominal_cohorts,
       ROUND(EXP(r.beta), 2) AS odds_ratio,
       ROUND(r.mlog10p, 2) AS mlog10p,
       ROUND(r.mlog10_fdr_q, 2) AS mlog10_fdr_q,
       r.phaplo, r.ptriplo
FROM rcnv_gene_associations_v r
JOIN phenotypes_v p ON p.dataset = r.dataset AND p.trait_original = r.phenotype
WHERE r.symbol = 'SHANK3' AND r.beta IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY r.mlog10_fdr_q DESC
LIMIT 20
```

### Deletion versus duplication of one gene, side by side per phenotype. A gene can be dosage sensitive in one direction only, and the two rows per phenotype are the way to see it.

```sql
SELECT phenotype,
       ROUND(MAX(IF(cnv_type = 'DEL', EXP(beta), NULL)), 2) AS del_or,
       ROUND(MAX(IF(cnv_type = 'DEL', mlog10_fdr_q, NULL)), 2) AS del_mlog10_fdr_q,
       ROUND(MAX(IF(cnv_type = 'DUP', EXP(beta), NULL)), 2) AS dup_or,
       ROUND(MAX(IF(cnv_type = 'DUP', mlog10_fdr_q, NULL)), 2) AS dup_mlog10_fdr_q
FROM rcnv_gene_associations_v
WHERE symbol = 'NRXN1' AND beta IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY phenotype
ORDER BY GREATEST(IFNULL(del_mlog10_fdr_q, 0), IFNULL(dup_mlog10_fdr_q, 0)) DESC
LIMIT 20
```

### Genes significantly associated with intellectual disability (HP:0001249) at the paper's own FDR-tier threshold: FDR < 1% (mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01)) AND (nominal evidence in at least two cohorts OR the leave-top-cohort-out secondary p-value still nominally significant). The exome-wide tier (mlog10p > -LOG10(2.90e-6)) with the same secondary-evidence requirement is the other way a gene qualifies. Thresholding on mlog10_fdr_q or mlog10p alone would not reproduce the published list.

```sql
SELECT symbol, ensembl_gene_id, cnv_type, n_nominal_cohorts,
       ROUND(EXP(beta), 2) AS odds_ratio,
       ROUND(mlog10p, 2) AS mlog10p,
       ROUND(mlog10_fdr_q, 2) AS mlog10_fdr_q,
       phaplo, ptriplo
FROM rcnv_gene_associations_v
WHERE phenotype = 'HP0001249'
  AND mlog10_fdr_q > -LOG10(0.01)
  AND (n_nominal_cohorts >= 2 OR mlog10p_secondary > -LOG10(0.05))
ORDER BY mlog10_fdr_q DESC
LIMIT 50
```

### Haploinsufficient genes that both carry a DEL association and sit in a fine-mapped region for a FinnGen trait. This view has no coordinates, so the GRCh38 interval comes from gene_annotations_v; the CTE's chr BETWEEN 1 AND 22 is what prunes credible_sets_v's chr partitions — rcnv_gene_associations_v only covers autosomal genes, so any chrX/Y credible set could never join anyway.

```sql
WITH cs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT chr, pos, trait_original, variant, pip
  FROM credible_sets_v
  WHERE resource = 'finngen' AND data_type = 'GWAS'
    AND trait_original = 'K11_IBD_STRICT' AND pip > 0.1
    AND chr BETWEEN 1 AND 22
)
SELECT r.symbol, g.chr, g.gene_start, g.gene_end, cs.variant, cs.pip,
       r.phenotype, ROUND(EXP(r.beta), 2) AS del_odds_ratio,
       ROUND(r.mlog10_fdr_q, 2) AS mlog10_fdr_q, r.phaplo
FROM cs
JOIN gene_annotations_v g
  ON g.chr = cs.chr AND cs.pos BETWEEN g.gene_start AND g.gene_end
JOIN rcnv_gene_associations_v r USING (ensembl_gene_id)
WHERE r.cnv_type = 'DEL' AND r.haploinsufficient AND r.beta IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY r.mlog10_fdr_q DESC
LIMIT 20
```
